name: Mixed-Media Animation
visualIdentity: Combine photography, drawings, paper, type, and optional 3D under shared color, line, texture, lighting, and composition rules. Give each medium a narrative role while keeping its material identity. The label does not establish physical stop-motion.
suitableUses: Explicit fit: product or editorial introductions, explanatory narratives, and abstract or cinematic sequences. Also suits documentary stories and research summaries when supplied photos and sketches can share visual rules. Interactive HTML can use scroll-stepped panels or image galleries; these are inferred applications.
limitations: May be too elaborate for very short topics. Chapter transitions can obscure cause or imply unexplained scene changes; cuts may conflict with continuous-shot or loop needs. Avoid distortion when it harms calm scenes or communication. No intrinsic palette or fixed audio style is specified.
palette: No canonical palette is specified. Optional example: paper #F1E6D1 background, ink #3B4948 foreground, accents #688E87 and #B97A5C; four discrete colors, no gradient. Exact task, brand, reference, semantic, and source-art colors take precedence. Accents fail the stated normal-text contrast target on paper; use ink on paper and check actual composites. Do not recolor source media automatically.
motionAndInteraction: Connect media with intentional transitions and coherent authored movement, preserving deliberate cuts, impacts, and reading holds. Optional chapter handoffs and scroll-driven story states need readable endpoints and synchronized copy; backward and direct seeks must remain coherent. Glitch is only for deliberately abrasive transitions. HTML may use finite scroll progress, reduced-motion behavior, accessible captions, or small parallax offsets; live pointer and scroll input is not for exported video. Use one owner per animated property.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; honor supplied requirements and assets. Synchronize and mix with picture, preserving speech intelligibility and avoiding clipping.
assetRequirements: Prepare photos, drawings, and paper for consistent color, edges, and dimensions; prerender 3D as transparent sequences when needed. Preserve originals and crop recipes. Rough.js can add seeded contours or hachure, but does not provide handwriting, authentic media, paper texture, or poses. Galleries need image dimensions, responsive sources, alternatives, and keyboard navigation.
combinations: Use alone when the media already shares rules. Optional style-024 annotations can connect details using consistent handwriting and approved colors; optional style-101 restrained parallax can separate narrative planes. Keep depth shallow and avoid revealing blank canvas. These are bounded suggestions, not requirements.
productionApproach: Select visual and motion methods by style, assets, action, and fidelity. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, synchronization, validation, and export pipeline; Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, with reason recorded. PixiJS is optional 2D layering; Pillow or Sharp preprocess assets, and Python supports asset work. Drive all rendered state from seekable composition time, preload assets, seed randomness, cache state, and inspect decoded frames and audio. Interactive-only tools include PhotoSwipe for image lightboxes, Cropper.js for non-destructive crop authoring, and Dragula for card reordering—not video animation.
